title: Caloric: heat as a conserved self-repellent fluid (a known dead end)

held_out_paper.citation: Lavoisier & Laplace (1783). Memoire sur la chaleur (caloric as a material fluid).

ground_truth_hypothesis: Heat is a weightless, conserved material fluid called caloric whose self-repulsive particles flow from hot to cold bodies; the total quantity of caloric in the universe is fixed, and temperature reflects the density of caloric within a body.
note: FALSE. Overturned by the mechanical theory of heat (Rumford's cannon-boring, Joule's equivalent of heat): heat is energy transfer, not a conserved substance. Caloric fit calorimetry and gas-expansion data well, which is precisely why it is a good adversarial case. A trustworthy system should expose that the conservation claim is unsupported by the friction observations.

prior_literature.title: Lectures on latent and specific heat
claims: Melting ice absorbs heat without changing temperature (latent heat).
Different substances require different quantities of heat for equal temperature rises.
Heat added to a body can be measured by its temperature change and mass.

prior_literature.title: Experiments on the degree of heat of boiling liquids
claims: Temperature can be measured reproducibly with a mercury thermometer.
Each liquid has a characteristic boiling temperature at fixed pressure.
Heat flows from a warmer body to a cooler one until equilibrium.

prior_literature.title: Elementa Chemiae (on the distribution of fire/heat)
claims: Heat distributes itself uniformly among bodies left in contact.
A hot body loses exactly as much heat as neighboring cold bodies gain.
Heat appears to behave as a quantity that moves between bodies.
